status: engineering draft — pending expert validation, will be revised by coaches. Ids are stable within v0-draft; coach corrections produce v1 with a recorded mapping.

faults.name: Late contact
faults.description: Ball is struck later than intended relative to the body, jamming the stroke.
faults.observableEvidence: At the contact frame the ball is level with or behind the torso midline instead of out front.

faults.name: Off-balance base
faults.description: The base is unstable through the hit; balance, not the ball, becomes the problem.
faults.observableEvidence: Feet still moving at contact, torso lean, stumble or hop immediately after the hit.

faults.name: Eyes leave the ball
faults.description: Head/gaze pulls off the contact zone before the ball is struck.
faults.observableEvidence: In the frames before contact the chin/gaze visibly turns toward the target early.

faults.name: No recovery to ready
faults.description: After the follow-through the player does not return paddle and base to a neutral ready position.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle hangs low / player static while the opponent strikes the next ball.

faults.name: Other (see rationale)
faults.description: Anything the draft vocabulary cannot express. The free-text rationale is the record.
faults.observableEvidence: Cite timestamps in the rationale; this is how the taxonomy grows from coach language.

faults.name: Wristy flick
faults.description: Wrist snaps through contact instead of a stable paddle face pushed from the shoulder.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle face angle changes rapidly in the frames around contact while the forearm barely moves.

faults.name: Backswing too big
faults.description: Take-back exceeds the compact dink envelope, costing control and time.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle travels behind the hip/torso plane before moving forward.

faults.name: Standing tall (no leg bend)
faults.description: Player bends at the wrist/back instead of loading the legs to get under the ball.
faults.observableEvidence: Knees near straight at contact on a below-net ball; torso hinges down instead.

faults.name: Contact not out front
faults.description: Ball is played beside or behind the body instead of in front of the front knee.
faults.observableEvidence: At contact the paddle is inside/behind the front knee line.

faults.name: Lifted, attackable trajectory
faults.description: Upward flick sends the ball high over the net where it can be attacked.
faults.observableEvidence: Outgoing arc apexes well above the net tape (visible against the net in frame).

faults.name: Paddle drops between dinks
faults.description: Paddle falls below knee height between contacts instead of resetting in front.
faults.observableEvidence: Between dinks the paddle head is visibly below the knees / pointing at the ground.

faults.name: Take-back beyond the shoulder
faults.description: Punch volley is wound up like a groundstroke; no time to recover at NVZ pace.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle drawn behind the shoulder plane before the forward move.

faults.name: Low ready paddle
faults.description: Paddle carried below net height at the NVZ, so high balls arrive before the paddle does.
faults.observableEvidence: Between volleys the paddle head is below the tape while the player is at the line.

faults.name: Wrist breaks down at contact
faults.description: Wrist collapses under pace; the face flips and the ball leaves off-line.
faults.observableEvidence: Abrupt face-angle change exactly at ball arrival; rebound direction inconsistent with face before contact.

faults.name: No split step
faults.description: Feet are not set when the opponent strikes, so the first move is late.
faults.observableEvidence: Player mid-stride (weight on one foot) at the opponent's contact frame.

faults.name: Overswing / long follow-through
faults.description: Volley finishes like a drive; compactness is lost and recovery is late.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle continues far across the body after contact instead of stopping in front.

faults.name: Contact low and late
faults.description: Ball taken beside the torso below net height instead of out front at the highest comfortable point.
faults.observableEvidence: Contact frame shows paddle below tape height and level with the torso.

faults.name: No unit turn
faults.description: Shoulders/hips never coil; preparation is arm-only.
faults.observableEvidence: Shoulder line stays square to the net through the backswing.

faults.name: Late preparation
faults.description: Paddle is not back before the bounce; the swing is rushed.
faults.observableEvidence: Backswing still moving backward at/after the ball's bounce frame.

faults.name: Arm-only power
faults.description: Kinetic chain skipped: hips/torso do not rotate into contact.
faults.observableEvidence: Hips visibly static while the arm accelerates; belt buckle never turns toward target.

faults.name: Weight stuck on the back foot
faults.description: Weight moves backward (or never forward) through contact.
faults.observableEvidence: Rear-leaning torso at contact; back foot loaded or stepping away.

faults.name: Open face at contact
faults.description: Paddle face open at impact; ball sails high/long.
faults.observableEvidence: Slow-motion contact frame shows face angled skyward; outgoing flight climbs.

faults.name: Incomplete follow-through
faults.description: Swing decelerates into/at contact instead of finishing across the body.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle stops shortly after the contact frame; no finish over shoulder/across torso.

faults.name: No sideways turn
faults.description: Body stays square to the net; the overhead becomes an arm wave.
faults.observableEvidence: Chest faces the net for the whole motion; no hip/shoulder line rotation sideways.

faults.name: Ball drifts behind the head
faults.description: Contact point ends up behind the head instead of up-and-slightly-in-front.
faults.observableEvidence: At contact the ball is above/behind the head plane; back arches to reach it.

faults.name: Dropped elbow
faults.description: Hitting elbow collapses below the shoulder before acceleration; power and reach are lost.
faults.observableEvidence: Elbow visibly below the shoulder line as the paddle starts forward.

faults.name: No off-hand tracking
faults.description: Non-paddle arm never points at / tracks the lob, so spacing is a guess.
faults.observableEvidence: Off arm hangs at the side during the setup instead of raising toward the ball.

faults.name: Feet never get under the ball
faults.description: Player reaches from where they stand instead of repositioning under the lob.
faults.observableEvidence: Zero adjustment steps between the lob going up and the swing.

faults.name: Off-balance landing
faults.description: Player falls backward/sideways after the smash and cannot play the next ball.
faults.observableEvidence: Backward stumble or hop after contact; no balanced landing.

families.displayName: Serves (technique only — legality is Serve Check, a separate concept)

faults.name: Inconsistent drop/toss
faults.description: Ball release point wanders serve to serve, so contact must chase it.
faults.observableEvidence: Across serves the release/drop point visibly differs relative to the stance.

faults.name: Arm-only serve
faults.description: No leg drive or weight transfer; all pace comes from the shoulder.
faults.observableEvidence: Hips static, back foot never releases through the strike.

faults.name: No unit turn
faults.description: Shoulders/hips do not coil during preparation.
faults.observableEvidence: Shoulder line square to the target through the whole motion.

faults.name: Rushed motion
faults.description: No settled routine; the serve is hit hurried and off-rhythm.
faults.observableEvidence: Almost no pause between setup and strike; off-balance finish.

faults.name: Contact point wanders
faults.description: Contact varies between out-front and beside-the-hip across serves.
faults.observableEvidence: Comparing serve contact frames shows widely different paddle/ball positions.

faults.name: Incomplete follow-through
faults.description: Motion decelerates at contact instead of finishing toward the target.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle stops near waist height right after contact.

faults.name: No split step at serve contact
faults.description: Returner is flat-footed or mid-stride when the serve is struck.
faults.observableEvidence: At the server's contact frame the returner's feet are not set/split.

faults.name: Overswing against pace
faults.description: Full groundstroke swing against a fast serve instead of a compact block/drive.
faults.observableEvidence: Long take-back past the torso plane against a visibly fast serve.

faults.name: Jammed contact
faults.description: Body not cleared; the ball plays the returner at the hip/torso.
faults.observableEvidence: Elbow pinned against the torso at contact; no space between body and paddle.

faults.name: No forward transition
faults.description: Returner stays parked at the baseline after the return instead of advancing.
faults.observableEvidence: Several frames after contact the returner has not started moving up-court.

faults.name: Overpowered arc
faults.description: Drop is driven flat/deep instead of apexing on the hitter's side and dying in the kitchen.
faults.observableEvidence: Ball apex occurs at/beyond the net plane; landing deep past the NVZ.

faults.name: Wrist scoop
faults.description: Wrist scoops the lift instead of a stable face lifted from shoulder/legs.
faults.observableEvidence: Face angle rotates through contact; wrist visibly hinges upward.

faults.name: No leg lift
faults.description: All arm on the lift; legs never load, so height control is inconsistent.
faults.observableEvidence: Knees straight through the lift on a low ball.

faults.name: Stiff hands on the reset
faults.description: Punching at a defensive reset instead of absorbing pace with soft hands.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle moves forward into the ball on a defensive reset; rebound too hot.

faults.name: Telegraphed wind-up
faults.description: Attack is announced by a visibly different preparation than the dink pattern.
faults.observableEvidence: Distinct pause/backswing before the attack that did not exist on previous dinks.

faults.name: Attack initiated below net height
faults.description: Speed-up attempted on a ball below the tape — low-percentage, rises into counters.
faults.observableEvidence: Contact frame shows the ball clearly below net height at initiation.

faults.name: No reset after the attack
faults.description: Player admires the speed-up instead of returning to ready for the counter.
faults.observableEvidence: Paddle/base not back to neutral by the opponent's counter contact.
